fields.Name: ORD-19 - Concurrency
fields.Description: What happens when two people confirm an order at the same instant (CN1-CN6). OrderNumber is an A/R document number and D30 makes two promises about it that nothing else in the suite tests: numbers are gap-conscious (a confirm that rolls back releases its number rather than burning it) and they are unique under contention. Both live in one small piece of SQL - UPDATE OrderSequence WITH (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK). Take the hints off and nothing visibly changes: every other check still passes, because they run one at a time. Two simultaneous confirms then read the same value and the second dies on the unique index, or - if that index were ever dropped - two customers share an invoice number. So these checks use a SECOND CONNECTION: ctx.Pool is a raw mssql pool, and a transaction taken from it is genuinely independent of the MJ provider's, which lets a check hold the counter row and watch a real confirm block on it. What this does NOT cover, stated plainly: two MJ confirms running at literally the same moment, since the suite has one provider - the competing actor is raw SQL performing the identical counter protocol.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: A confirm blocks while another session holds the counter and resumes at the NEXT number rather than the one already taken; the counter advances by exactly one per number issued; a confirm that rolls back (a CoC line with no GL links) leaves the counter exactly where it found it, so no A/R document number is burned; the database refuses a second order carrying an existing number; the payment counter serializes identically, proving the hints were not dropped from one of the two copies; and two reversal lines saved together against one origin are refused when their SUM exceeds it while a legitimate 2 + 1 split against a 3-unit sale still books.
